focus: the record, bridge, diff, bench, shadow and gate method — and which parts apply to any Rust port checked against an original
noveltyJustification: All 15 findings are new to the packet: none of the gate checks, cheat guard, size ratio, shadow stage or pitfall rules appeared in iteration 1, and each is paired with a sk-code coverage verdict.
keyQuestions: What are rust-anything's record, bridge, diff, bench, shadow and gate methods (docs/how-it-works.md), docs/pitfalls.md and DECISIONS.md, and which of them apply to any Rust port checked against an original?
ruledOut: Reading gate as a single command
Treating bench as a gate check

label: The method is a nine-step pipeline with a named owner per step and the original as the oracle; sk-code states the byte-parity acceptance bar but never the record-then-replay method that produces the evidence
gate is a composite of named Check values each carrying a fix hint, so a failure names the command that repairs it; sk-code lists the three commands but has no check-reports-its-remedy notion

The cheat guard is the highest-value transferable rule: literals, tests and recording checks catch a port that passes diff by hard-coding results, deleting failing tests or editing the recording; sk-code has no equivalent and recorded-literal appears zero times

The size ceiling is a ratio with an allowance, Rust no more than 3x the original's lines plus 50, and the failure message explains that over-growth means hand-rolled crate code; sk-code has no size rule

unsafe is audited for an explanation, every use needing a SAFETY comment immediately above; sk-code already requires this in 6 reference files and 2 checklist files, so the two agree and the rule must not be duplicated

bench is deliberately outside gate because speed is not correctness but decides whether a port ships, and every x18n core port was correct and slower; sk-code mentions bench but never states the separation

Shadow mode is a fourth verification stage after the gate: run both, return the original's result, never let a Rust error reach a caller, selected by RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old|shadow|new; shadow appears zero times in the sk-code Rust set

Two precise parity rules: both sides throwing counts as agreement, and error messages are not compared; sk-code has an error_parity test in its inventory but never says what counts as agreement on the error path

The comparison codec is lossless on purpose and its value list is the harness checklist: undefined, NaN, -0, BigInt, Map/Set, key order, lone surrogates; sk-code has the same contract in different words but not the named value list

preserve_order is a correctness feature with a measured cost and a feature-unification trap: Cargo unifies it across the binary so every serde_json::Value lookup hashes the key, and a vector-backed value type made the printer 1.7x faster; sk-code mentions neither

Compile regexes once with OnceLock and know that serde_json::Map::remove reorders keys under preserve_order and that JS string comparison is UTF-16 while Rust str ordering is UTF-8; OnceLock, shift_remove and UTF-16 appear zero times in the sk-code Rust set

The repository documents what its method cannot prove as a first-class section: inputs nobody recorded, an original that moved on, regexes, run-to-run change, floats, anything not in the output, other platforms; sk-code's parity section is all obligation and no limit

Corrections are kept in a committed rust/RULES.md, one bullet each, injected into every prompt the tool writes; sk-code is itself the rule file so the mechanism is unneeded but the instruction to record a mid-port correction is missing

docs/pitfalls.md is a rule-per-mistake ledger with a standing instruction to add to it in the same change; sk-code states rules without the incident that produced them, and a rule with its failure attached is followed where a rule alone is argued with

Every published number is measured and the measurement conditions are part of the number: quiet machine, run twice, name the hardware and core count, include the slow cases, no rounding up; sk-code has no rule for stating a performance claim

direction: Reading gate as a single command
reason: gate.rs is a dispatcher that pushes a Check per concern and returns a GateOutcome; the checks are the unit of design, not the command

direction: Treating bench as a gate check
reason: DECISIONS.md:59 says explicitly that bench is a separate step and gives the reason: speed is not correctness but decides whether a port ships

direction: Deriving the cheat guard from the diff step
reason: diff compares recorded cases and cannot see that the port hard-coded them; the guard needs a separate comparison against the original's source text and a saved test baseline

label: grep -ril cheat over the sk-code Rust references returns one false positive, the heading NAMING CHEAT SHEET in quick-reference/naming-ordering-and-signatures.md:33; distinctive-token probes are the reliable coverage test
